trends.name: Grok Build apps exposed public data
trends.summary: Security researchers say many Grok Build apps can be accessed without logging in, including patient data and plaintext passwords.
trends.attention_driver: Low-code agents increase deployment speed, while also increasing errors in default permissions and data publishing configurations.

evidence.quote: more than 35,000 Grok-built apps open to anyone without login, including patient data
evidence.claim: Supports reports of unauthenticated access and sensitive data exposure across many apps.

evidence.quote: 35,000 Grok Build apps wide open to anyone who looked for them.
evidence.claim: Supports the exposure incident receiving attention from another media outlet.

trends.so_what: Make public access, secret scanning and sensitive data detection hard gates before generative apps are released. Independently audit backend configurations generated by agents. Do not treat runnable code as ready for production.

trends.name: AlphaProof Code demonstrates large-scale formal software verification
trends.summary: DeepMind says AlphaProof Code verified Signal's core encryption code with three million lines of Lean proofs.
trends.attention_driver: The delivery cycle for verifiable code has been compressed, drawing more attention to automated review for high-risk software.

evidence.quote: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.
evidence.claim: Supports that AlphaProof Code has been used to verify Signal's core encryption implementation.

evidence.quote: verified Signal's cryptographic core in four weeks instead of years
evidence.claim: Supports external reports that the verification cycle was significantly shortened.

trends.so_what: Product promises for coding agents should distinguish between "generation" and "verifiable delivery". Configure formal checks or reproducible evidence for high-risk changes. Reliability will affect enterprise procurement more than code output volume alone.

trends.name: Gemini 4 Carbon opens to developers and users
trends.summary: Google announced that Gemini 4 Carbon is available and expanded access to developers, enterprises and Gemini App users.
trends.attention_driver: Broader availability of a flagship model is driving comparisons of pricing and coding workflows.

evidence.claim: Supports that Gemini 4 Carbon is officially available.

evidence.quote: 谷歌Gemini新旗舰全面上线，一夜复刻OpenCode桌面应用
evidence.claim: Supports that the release has prompted discussion about developer workflows.

trends.so_what: Include Gemini 4 Carbon in selection tests using real tasks, with a focus on complex programming and multi-step work quality. Do not switch models based on rankings alone. Also measure latency, failure recovery and cost per task.

watch_list.name: Google TPU 8 expands inference deployment options
watch_list.summary: Reports focus on Google adjusting TPU accelerators to support a broader range of inference workloads, with different memory and confidential computing configurations.
watch_list.attention_driver: Inference deployments depend more on memory bandwidth, host configuration and data isolation capabilities.

evidence.quote: Google Rejiggers TPU Accelerators For Broader AI Inference Work
evidence.claim: Supports Google adjusting TPU products to cover a broader range of inference workloads.
Supports that TPU 8 series configurations emphasize memory bandwidth and confidential computing.

watch_list.so_what: If a product is constrained by long-context or high-concurrency costs, procurement evaluations should include non-GPU options. Compare throughput, tail latency and data isolation in the same load test, rather than looking only at single-model speed.

insights.text: Verifiable delivery enters procurement metrics: delivery evaluations for high-risk code will place more weight on reproducible proofs than generation volume
Generative apps need release gates: default public configurations turn low-code development speed directly into data leak risk
Agent tools are still expanding: new signals for containerization and lightweight frameworks reached 5
